clue.text: Go over a lot of nonsense

indicators.note: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: tripe is rubbish talk

explanation.surface: Someone told to review a heap of drivel.
explanation.walkthrough: TRIPE loses its last letter to give TRIP; 'Go over' looks like 'review', but here it means fall over.
explanation.definitionFit: To trip is to stumble and fall, which is one sense of going over.

clue.text: Confectionery name incomplete: different name taken up

indicators.note: something incomplete is missing its end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a noun is a naming word

indicators.note: in a down entry, something taken up is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a tag is another word for a name or label

explanation.surface: A sweet's brand name is half-finished, and a new one is adopted instead.
explanation.walkthrough: NOUN loses its last letter to give NOU, and TAG is read upwards as GAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Nougat is a chewy sweet made from sugar or honey, nuts and egg white, an example of confectionery.

clue.text: Old German man blocking military vehicles and soldiers

parts.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old

indicators.note: something blocking a passage sits inside it, so these letters go within the vehicles

parts.note: tanks are armoured military vehicles
Herr is the German for Mr, a man

explanation.surface: An elderly German stands in the way of a convoy of tanks and troops.
explanation.walkthrough: Herr is the German equivalent of Mr; 'other ranks' is the British army's term for those below officer rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Other ranks is the British military term for enlisted soldiers who are not commissioned officers.

clue.text: Endless party, no longer fresh, showing devastation

indicators.note: endless means without its end, so the final letter is removed

parts.note: a rave is a large dance party
something aged is old, not new

explanation.surface: A party that never stops leaves its revellers jaded and the venue wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no longer fresh' reads as part of the party scene, but it is a separate piece meaning old.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravaged describes something laid waste or badly damaged, so it shows the effects of devastation.

clue.text: Loud song of reasonable quality

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical marking for loud
an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: A noisy song that is passable but nothing special.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair means moderately good, adequate but not outstanding, as in a school mark.

clue.text: Stops senior officer getting head of detectives to probe crime information

parts.note: OC is Officer Commanding

indicators.note: a probe pushes inside something, so this letter goes within the other piece

parts.note: clues are pieces of evidence in a crime

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of detectives

explanation.surface: A senior officer halts a case by sending in the chief detective to examine the evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: OC, Officer Commanding, is the usual crossword senior officer.
explanation.definitionFit: To occlude is to block or close off, so occludes is a formal synonym for stops.

clue.text: Copper advanced, stopping short, interrupting cessation of hostilities and aggression?

indicators.note: to interrupt something is to break into the middle of it

parts.note: a truce is an agreed halt to fighting

indicators.note: stopping short means not reaching the end, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
advanced as in lent money

explanation.surface: A policeman pushes forward but halts, breaking up a ceasefire — is that aggressive?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is the metal; 'advanced' is the money sense, as in a loan.
explanation.definitionFit: Truculence is an eagerness to fight or argue, a defiant aggressiveness of manner.

clue.text: A river's name, nothing more

parts.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for river
N is the abbreviation for name
O, the zero, is nothing

explanation.surface: Just the name of a river, nothing else.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue both builds the letters one by one and describes the result: the answer is simply a river's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arno is the river that flows through Florence and Pisa in Tuscany.

clue.text: A scoundrel nipping back to snatch one item of jewellery

indicators.note: going back means the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to snatch something is to grab and hold it, so this piece holds the next

parts.note: a rat is a contemptible person
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A villain darts back to grab a piece of jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: A RAT reads backwards as TARA, which then holds I.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled ornamental headband, a piece of jewellery worn on the head.

clue.text: Grant, perhaps — college horde squandering millions

parts.note: C is a common abbreviation for college

indicators.note: squandering something means losing it, so that letter is thrown away

parts.note: an army is a vast crowd
M stands for million

explanation.surface: A grant to a college wasted by a mob of students spending millions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grant' poses as funding but is the film star Cary Grant. ARMY minus M gives ARY.
explanation.definitionFit: Cary is the first name of the Hollywood actor Cary Grant, so Grant is an example of a Cary.

clue.text: A US writer penning good English? That's the remotest thing

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as in a pen, so one piece wraps around another

parts.note: taken as written
Edgar Allan Poe, American author
G is the abbreviation for good
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: An American author writing proper English seems the most unlikely thing of all.
explanation.walkthrough: POE holds G, with A in front and E after.
explanation.definitionFit: The apogee is the point in an orbit furthest from the Earth, hence the most distant or highest point.

clue.text: Scary shifts, covering most of lap in synthetic fibres

indicators.note: covering means going around, so the rearranged letters wrap the other piece
shifts means moves about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its last letter

parts.note: to lap is to lick up with the tongue

explanation.surface: Frightening work shifts on the factory floor, part of a lap spent among man-made fibres.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lap' is the verb, as a cat laps milk, not a circuit of a track.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrylics are synthetic fibres or fabrics made from acrylic polymers, used in knitwear.

clue.text: Certainly uncommonly teary about Queen in the past

definitions.note: the answer is a noun, the past itself, while the definition is a phrase meaning formerly

parts.note: yes affirms, like certainly

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so these letters go around the monarch
uncommonly means in an unusual way, so these letters take an unusual order

parts.note: anagram fodder
ER, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Certainly, an unusually tearful moment regarding a monarch long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the standard crossword Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Yesteryear means time gone by, former years, so of yesteryear is equivalent to belonging to the past.

clue.text: Lovely gumshoe given to baseball player

definitions.note: a lovely here is a noun, an attractive person

parts.note: a private eye is a detective, a gumshoe
the catcher crouches behind home plate

explanation.surface: A detective is drawn to an attractive baseball player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lovely' reads as an adjective but serves as a noun, an attractive person; gumshoe is American slang for a detective.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye-catcher is something or someone strikingly attractive, as is a lovely, a pretty person.

clue.text: Hobby developed into career

indicators.note: something developed has been worked into a new form, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: anagram fodder, both words together

explanation.surface: A pastime that grew into a profession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' looks like a link word but its letters are part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A recreation is an activity pursued for enjoyment in leisure time, which is what a hobby is.

clue.text: Store that's invested in modelling in America?

indicators.note: something invested in a thing is placed inside it, so only the interior letters are kept

parts.note: the American spelling has a single L, and its middle four letters are kept

explanation.surface: A shop that has put money into the US fashion industry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in America' asks for the US spelling with one L; the British spelling with two would not work, which is why the setter adds it.
explanation.definitionFit: A deli, short for delicatessen, is a shop selling cooked meats and fine foods, so a type of store.

clue.text: Particle captured suddenly after one escapes

indicators.note: when one escapes, a letter standing for one leaves the phrase

parts.note: leapt on, pounced on

explanation.surface: A tiny particle is suddenly trapped after another escapes.
explanation.walkthrough: LEAPT ON loses A, a word for one, to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A lepton is a subatomic particle, such as the electron or neutrino, that does not feel the strong force.

clue.text: Cross and abrupt about half of partying

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: terse means curt

indicators.note: half of a word keeps just its first two letters of four

parts.note: first half of rave, a word for partying

explanation.surface: An angry, short-tempered reveller, half in party mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' reads as angry, but it is the verb to go across. Partying is RAVE, and half of it is RAV.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse is to travel across or through something, so it is a verb meaning cross.

clue.text: Aircraft pilots heading off, having recalled answer

indicators.note: heading off means losing the head, so the first letter goes

parts.note: aces are expert fighter pilots

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: ans is the abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: Pilots set off after remembering the response they gave.
explanation.walkthrough: ACES loses A, and ANS is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Cessna is an American maker of light aircraft, so a Cessna is a small plane.

clue.text: Riotous overture for concert penned by composer, I see

indicators.note: penned by means written inside, so this letter goes within the composer

parts.note: J S Bach, German composer

indicators.note: an overture opens a piece, so only the first letter is taken

parts.note: first letter of concert
I + C, see as the letter C

explanation.surface: A rowdy concert opening written by a composer, as far as I can tell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I see' is read as the letters I and C, the letter C sounding like see.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacchic means drunken and wild, from Bacchus, Roman god of wine and revelry.

clue.text: Can start to accommodate molten material

parts.note: can is slang for a toilet, as is lav

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of accommodate

explanation.surface: Can you begin to make room for melted stuff?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a verb but is US slang for a toilet; lav (lavatory) is the British word.
explanation.definitionFit: Lava is molten rock that flows from a volcano, cooling into solid stone.

clue.text: Fake vandalised? Not initially penitent

indicators.note: not initially means without the first letter

parts.note: a sham is a fake
defaced, spoilt by graffiti

explanation.surface: A forged painting, damaged — and its maker regretful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not initially' acts on the vandalised piece, not on the fake one.
explanation.definitionFit: Shamefaced means showing shame or embarrassment, which is how a penitent person looks.

clue.text: Think a lot of spot with quantity of mud

parts.note: an advertising spot on TV or radio
a mire is a stretch of swampy mud

explanation.surface: Someone pondering a spot of mud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spot' reads as a mark but is a commercial slot on air, an advert.
explanation.definitionFit: To admire someone is to regard them highly, to hold them in great esteem.

clue.text: Divers, full of excitement, abandoning river, circling cape

definitions.note: divers is an old adjective meaning various

indicators.note: circling means going around, so this piece surrounds another
abandoning means leaving behind, so that letter goes

parts.note: an electric atmosphere is thrilling
R stands for river
C is the abbreviation for cape

explanation.surface: Thrilled swimmers leave the river and round a headland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divers' looks like swimmers but is the old adjective meaning various. ELECTRIC drops R, then goes around C.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclectic means drawn from varied sources, so it matches divers in its old sense of assorted.

clue.text: Gutted the church and college

indicators.note: a gutted thing has lost its insides, leaving only the outside letters

parts.note: outer letters of the
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A church and college ruined by fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A tech is an informal name for a technical college, an institution of further education.

clue.text: Appropriate logo for company, perhaps involving one cathedral

indicators.note: involving means wrapping up within, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: TM, trademark
I is the Roman numeral one
Ely is an English cathedral city

explanation.surface: A fitting emblem for a firm that features a cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: A trademark symbol stands in for a company logo; Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Timely means happening at a suitable moment, so it is apt or appropriate.

clue.text: Meat? Happen to be tucking into pound

indicators.note: tucking into means going inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: lb is the abbreviation for a pound weight
I am, I happen to be

explanation.surface: Is that meat being eaten by the pound?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' looks like a currency but is the weight abbreviation LB; AM is the first-person form of 'be'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamb is the meat of young sheep, eaten roasted or as chops.

clue.text: Tries to avoid acting of the woman

indicators.note: to avoid something is to keep it out, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a judge hears or tries a case
A is the abbreviation for acting

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to dodge her performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tries' looks like attempts but it is the court sense, hears. A, for acting as in an acting role, comes out.
explanation.definitionFit: Hers is the possessive pronoun meaning belonging to her, that is, of the woman.

clue.text: Fabric swatch in orange, though not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely means only part of these words is used, within them

parts.note: letters running across these words

explanation.surface: A fabric sample that is orange, but not wholly so.
explanation.definitionFit: Chino is a strong twilled cotton cloth, used for casual trousers, so it is a fabric.

clue.text: Slopes deprived of soft sheep

indicators.note: deprived of means lacking, so that letter is removed

parts.note: ramps are slopes
p, piano, is the musical marking for soft

explanation.surface: Hillsides missing their sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Rams are male sheep, so the plural matches sheep.
